final_message:
I built the Nocturne landing page, but I couldn't build or view it: node and npm are blocked in this sandbox ("operation not permitted"), so neither `npm run build` nor `tsc` has run. The theses and the design system are also unvalidated, since nobody answered the gates.

## Direction (UNVALIDATED)

**Brainstorm answers (assumptions, from the brief):**
- The product: the hero is the real sky over Lisbon, the field the dome will show at 22:00 on Friday 9 October 2026.
- The audience: adults 20–40 choosing a night out.
- The mood: nocturnal, exact, quiet, unhurried.
- No references were given.
- The stack: React 19, Vite, vanilla CSS, no animation library.

**Visual thesis:** the page is the inside of the dome as the lights go down.
- **Colour:** near-black ground (`#05070a`), star-white text (`#e8ebf0`), and one accent, Saturn amber (`#e6c07b`), used only for Saturn and for booking.
- **Type:** the system sans. No web font can be requested here. The voice comes from huge light-weight times (21:30 / 22:00 / 23:30) with fixed-width figures, and small spaced capitals for coordinates.
- **Layout:** airy 8px spacing, sharp corners, thin rules, flat.
- **First screen:** the all-sky disc plotted from `data/stars.json`, with the zenith at the centre, north at the top and east at the left, as seen looking up. On a wide screen the disc takes the right side and the title, times and booking sit on the left.

**Interaction thesis:**
- Hovers take 160ms with `cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1)`, and nothing scales.
- Only the hero responds to scrolling. Twinkling, glows, bounce, fade-in reveals, constellation lines and anything not in the data are ruled out.
- **The one motion, "house lights down":** while the disc is held in place, scrolling dims the ground from dusk to night. Stars light in order of brightness, Vega, Capella and Saturn first, down to magnitude 4.5, with a counter of how many of the 403 stars are lit.
- With reduced motion on, the disc is not held, the ground is night, and every star is shown at once.

`Allowed patterns: a vertical dusk-to-night ground gradient in the hero; hairline rules; small letter-spaced uppercase labels for coordinates and times; a live scroll-linked star counter; tabular figures; a near-black ground.`

`Set aside: navy nebula space page; white museum page; deep-space imagery; antique star atlas. Kept: the dome's own projection (all-sky disc, zenith centre).`

**Style lookup dials:** variance 6, motion 3, density 3. From its proposal I kept the 150–300ms hover range and the 44px touch targets. I dropped its navy palette, waitlist layout with sign-up counts, Outfit/Work Sans fonts (they would need a font request nobody agreed to), glow, fade-in reveals, parallax and GSAP code.

**Content limits:** every figure on the page comes from the data or the brief. The Moon and the other planets are not drawn. The page never names the planetarium, credits the IAU star names, and links only to URLs listed in the data.

## Files
- `MASTER.md`: the design system and the theses.
- `src/tokens.css`: the colour, type, spacing and motion values.
- `src/sky.ts`: the sky projection, the order stars light in, and the star table.
- `src/SkyDome.tsx`: the hero.
- `src/App.tsx`: program, tonight's sky, practical information and data credits.
- `src/index.css`, `index.html`: styles, page title and description.
- `preview/theses.html`, `preview/design-system.html`: the previews, standalone.

No dependency was added, and none was needed. Bunshin was not proposed because this is one page, not a whole site.

## Audit

**First screen, read from the code:**
- `First screen:` the all-sky disc of 403 stars plus Saturn (`src/SkyDome.tsx:94`), with the title, times and "Book tickets" link (`src/SkyDome.tsx:78`).
- `Width and edges:` at 64rem and wider, the text column takes the measure plus the gutter and the disc takes the rest (`src/index.css:291`). The hero now uses the same 80rem frame as the sections (`src/index.css:178`), so the left edges line up.
- `The one motion:` the scroll handler (`src/SkyDome.tsx:43`), the per-star fade (`src/index.css` `.star`), and the dusk overlay fading out as you scroll.

**Checked here: 11 checks, 2 problems found.**
- **Important: star names on the disc are too small on phones.** They are 26 SVG units, which comes to about 7px on a 375px screen. They are hidden from screen readers and the same stars appear in the table, but they are hard to read.
- **Nice to have: a few hard-coded values instead of tokens.** These are the SVG text sizes (24/26) and stroke widths (1.5) in `src/index.css:228–257`, the heading line-height 1.1, the label letter-spacing 0.1em and 0.04em, the disabled opacity 0.4, and the layout sizes 22rem, 13rem, 12rem and 16rem.
- **Thesis against code: pass.**
  - Hover timing: 160ms at `tokens.css:58`, easing at `:59`, used at `index.css:112` and `:129`.
  - Palette: `tokens.css:6–14`.
  - Star tint and Saturn: `SkyDome.tsx:16`.
  - Time numerals: `index.css:89`.
  - One change from the preview: the disc is held in its own scroll stage, so it fits on a phone.
- **Reduced motion: pass.** `tokens.css:70` drops the scroll length and the transitions, `index.css:304` stops the hero holding in place, and `SkyDome.tsx:45` shows every star at once.
- **Exit animations: not applicable.** Nothing on the page appears or disappears conditionally.
- **No layout-property animation: pass.** The audit script found none; only opacity changes.
- **Focus visible: pass.** `index.css:154–155`, and there is no `outline: none`.
- **All five states: pass** for the button and the link: hover is gated to pointer devices, plus active, focus and disabled (`index.css:115–155`).
- **Contrast: pass.**
  - Body text `#e8ebf0` on `#05070a`: 16.88:1.
  - Secondary text `#9aa3b0` on `#05070a`: 7.91:1, and 6.02:1 on the dusk colour.
  - Button text `#05070a` on `#e6c07b`: 11.71:1, and 13.98:1 on hover.
  - Horizon ring `#5d6672`: 3.47:1.
- **Semantics: pass.** The disc is an image with a title and description (`SkyDome.tsx:97`). Individual stars are hidden from screen readers, and the data is a real table.
- **`will-change` / AnimatePresence:** none used, and none needed.
- **Tells against the thesis:** the script found 0 of 18 on its second pass.
  - I removed one problem I had introduced: eyebrow labels above sections, which the allowed list did not cover.
  - The script's `hover-no-transition` finding (`index.css:138`, `:144`) is **not this tell**: the transitions are on the base rules (`:112`, `:129`).
  - Allowed by the thesis: the hairline rules, the coordinate and time labels, the live star counter, and the dusk gradient.

**For you to run (UNVERIFIED): 5 checks.**

| What to run | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` (type check plus Vite build) | builds with no errors |
| Chrome DevTools > Performance while scrolling the hero | no frame over 16.7ms (about 400 stars re-styled on each frame) |
| The page at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440 widths, plus a short phone (667px tall) | no horizontal scroll, and the disc's caption not cut off while the disc is held in place |
| The page with the OS "reduce motion" setting on | no hold, night ground, all stars shown at once |
| A browser without `color-mix` support | stars still show, though without colour tint |

One thing for you to decide: the brief fixes the hero to Friday 9 October 2026, which is a month before today (13 November 2026).
